dedupe_keys.name: public transport network data sets for 25 cities kujala et al

description: This collection gives the public transport networks of 25 cities in easy-to-use formats derived from agencies' GTFS timetable feeds: network edge lists, temporal network event lists, SQLite databases, GeoJSON files and cleaned GTFS files, with stop-to-stop walking distances added from OpenStreetMap. Cities include Adelaide, Belfast, Berlin, Bordeaux, Brisbane, Canberra, Detroit, Dublin, Grenoble, Helsinki, Kuopio, Lisbon, Luxembourg, Melbourne, Nantes, Palermo, Paris, Prague, Rennes, Rome, Sydney, Toulouse, Turku, Venice and Winnipeg. It was compiled at Aalto University by Kujala, Weckström, Darst, Mladenović and Saramäki and described in Scientific Data (5:180089, 15 May 2018). Coverage is city scale: feeds were filtered to city bounds, week extracts cover a full week of operations and other extracts a typical Monday. The files are free on Zenodo (version 1.2, 28 February 2018, one zip per city of 20 to 316 MB); the processing pipeline and the gtfspy Python package are on GitHub under MIT. Caveats: the timetables date from 2017 and 2018, source feeds keep their own licences (for example CC BY 3.0 Italy), and the interactive repository site no longer answers. The data serve as a benchmark for network flow, routing, accessibility and resilience studies of transit networks, and relate to the GTFS specification and to feed catalogues such as Transitland catalogued here.
